verdict.analysis: A addresses more launch requirements, adding required consent, a client-side honeypot, and draft terms. B renders cleanly, while A’s supplied checkout renders are unstyled with missing-resource errors. Both retain novalidate, provide no backend validation or rate limiting, and replace the HTTP endpoint with a relative URL that does not enforce HTTPS. Neither delivers working payments. Both reports acknowledge blockers, but their claimed browser tests have no accompanying execution evidence. A additionally makes an unsafe claim that failed requests mean the customer was not charged. B invents workshop positioning beyond the supplied description. A wins narrowly on the specified requirements, despite its rendering defects and incomplete legal content.

criteria.note: Both forms explicitly retain novalidate; custom JavaScript validation does not enable native submission validation.
Both use required email inputs and check validity in their submission handlers.
A includes a required checkbox and checks acceptance before submitting. B has no terms acceptance control.
A includes a honeypot checked in JavaScript, but does not transmit it for server enforcement. B has none.
Both remove the explicit HTTP endpoint and use /api/pay, which inherits the page protocol. Neither guarantees HTTPS; A’s host-dependent HSTS configuration is unverified.
Neither delivers a server endpoint or server-side validation.
A supplies a linked terms page, but essential organizer and cancellation provisions remain placeholders. B supplies no terms page.
